newsitem.title: INDIA: Death toll in Indian rains rises to at least 92.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Indian rains rises to at least 92.

text.p: At least 92 people have died and thousands left homeless in floods that have ravaged large areas of southern India, officials said on Monday.

The coastal state of Andhra Pradesh has been worst affected after six days of torrential rain that have killed at least 75 people, destroyed thousands of mud houses and washed away vast areas of agricultural land.
Rains in Andhra Pradesh and neighbouring Tamil Nadu state have damaged railway tracks and bridges and uprooted trees.
Local people say the final death toll for both states could exceed 200.
More than 38,000 people, most of them farmers and fishermen, had been rescued by troops from low-lying coastal districts in both states, officials said.
Thunderstorms have snapped telephone lines, badly affecting rescue operations, which have also involved the Indian air force.
C.V.V. Bhadram, the director of the meteorological centre at Hyderabad, the state capital of Andhra Pradesh, said rains had now abated to a drizzle.
"The situation has improved substantially with the low pressure moving away from the state's mainland," Bhadram said.
Life in Tamil Nadu was slowly returning to normal with no rain reported in the past 24 hours.
"Most deaths occurred due to collapse of houses and electrocution," said an official in the state's agricultural ministry.
